axis: esm2_t33_650M_full_finetune phase kickoff: timing calibration (not a quality trial)
note: Pivot from esm2_t36_3B_lora_scaleup after two throughput-recovery attempts (removing gradient_checkpointing OOM'd; halving LoRA depth only recovered 11.8%, leaving trial-069 still ~122x slower per example than the esm2_t12_35M phase). esm2_t33_650M_UR50D is the largest ESM2 tier that fits FULL fine-tuning under the 25GB VRAM budget (~10.4GB for weights+grads+optimizer at the standard ~16 bytes/param mixed-precision-AdamW estimate, per the original three-way analysis) - this matches the old ProtBERT notebook's approach (full fine-tune of a big model) more directly than LoRA did, without LoRA's forward-pass-dominated compute ceiling. Uses --unfreeze-last-n 33 (all 33 layers - the non-LoRA path, not --use-lora) so every parameter is trainable, matching 'fully trainable' as requested. Mirrors trial-067's role: 200 train / 100 val examples, 1 epoch, to get real per-example throughput before committing to a properly-budgeted real trial. --gradient-checkpointing kept on as a cautious default given trial-068's OOM lesson (full fine-tuning of 650M params needs real weight+gradient+optimizer memory on top of activations, unlike LoRA's tiny trainable footprint) - verified locally beforehand that checkpointing works correctly on this fully-unfrozen path without needing LoRA's enable_input_require_grads() hook (no frozen boundary exists). weight_decay=0.2/output_dropout=0.2/learning_rate=2e-4 carried forward from esm2_t12_35M_coarse_go_terms's own findings as a starting point, not yet validated at this scale or fine-tuning mode.
